content: Co-fluampicil is the British Approved Name for a combination of two β-lactam antibiotics: ampicillin and flucloxacillin. This combination is marketed under the trade name Magnapen. Ampicillin is a penicillin-class antibiotic with a moderate spectrum of activity, providing effective coverage against Group A streptococcal infections. Flucloxacillin, on the other hand, is a narrow-spectrum antibiotic that is particularly effective against Staphylococcus aureus. The combination of these two antibiotics is specifically designed to target the two most common bacterial pathogens responsible for cellulitis infections in the extremities, such as the arms or legs. Co-fluampicil is available in several formulations, including capsules containing 250 mg of each component (Co-fluampicil 250/250), a syrup formulation with 125 mg of each component (Co-fluampicil 125/125), and a powder form (Co-fluampicil 250/250) that can be reconstituted for intravenous injection. The typical oral dosage for adults is one Co-fluampicil 250/250 capsule taken four times daily. In cases of severe infection, the dosage may be doubled. For children under the age of 10, the dosage is typically halved. The side effects of Co-fluampicil are consistent with those of its individual components. The most common adverse effect is gastrointestinal upset, particularly stomach or bowel discomfort, which is primarily associated with flucloxacillin. Both ampicillin and flucloxacillin belong to the penicillin family of antibiotics, so this medication should not be used by individuals with a known allergy to penicillin. Additional contraindications specific to flucloxacillin should also be reviewed before prescribing or administering this medication.
